extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers (U.S. public)
extracted.subtask_short: reporting postwar housing and security policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing U.S. post‑World War II policy measures: administration programs, regulations and appointments to address the housing shortage, procedures for releasing surplus property, and criteria for a national security reorganization. Includes statistics, recommended steps, and standards for acceptable security plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: To increase the supply of building materials
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) To increase the supply of building materials;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use priorities, allocations and special measures (man‑power recruiting, allocations of machinery and materials) to raise production; examples given include cast‑iron soil pipe increasing from 12,000 to 22,000 tons and bricks from 131,000,000 to 265,000,000 over months.

rubrics_metrics.name: To strengthen inventory controls to prevent hoarding
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) To strengthen inventory controls to prevent hoarding;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch inventories closely to prevent hoarding and assure prompt distribution of scarce materials; widening of these controls is being studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: To strengthen price controls over building materials
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) To strengthen price controls over building materials;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Price Administration placing local dollar‑and‑cents ceilings on construction materials and services; lumber price increases have been granted as a tool; rent controls are cited as a successful safeguard against housing inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: To discourage unsound lending practices and speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) To discourage unsound lending practices and speculation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit agencies to work out ways to curb unsound lending; discouraging speculative and unsound lending practices to prevent inflationary price rises in housing.

rubrics_metrics.name: To enlist industry support in increasing production and fighting inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) To enlist industry support in increasing production and fighting inflation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration to hold meetings with labor and management, home‑financing institutions and public‑interest groups (e.g., Dec. 17–18 meeting) to discuss methods of stimulating home construction at reasonable prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: To provide information and advisory service on home values to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) To provide information and advisory service on home values to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public information/advisory services are part of the six‑point program to help consumers and communities make informed housing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program for speeding up release of surplus housing units and building materials
rubrics_metrics.description: A program to speed up release of surplus government housing units and building materials held by the government so they are immediately available to states and local communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes making available Army and Navy barracks/dormitories (lend to communities for the duration of the emergency), moving/remodeling where necessary, special teams to locate surpluses and sell on the spot, arranging that at least 70% of released materials go into housing, estimated 100,000 units to become available, and appropriations requested to finance removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel ~50% of building materials to low‑cost housing (≤ $10,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulation to establish priorities for dwelling units costing $10,000 or less so that about 50 per cent of all building materials will be channeled into this type of building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance remaining materials for commercial, industrial, higher‑priced dwelling and other construction; regulation issued under the second war powers act; includes veterans' preference for purchase/rental of these units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide veterans preference in purchase or rental of housing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide preferences for veterans in the purchase or rental of housing so that they can buy or rent units before others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General statement that veterans receive preference for vacancies in all Federal housing units; reflected specifically in the low‑cost unit priority regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish ceiling prices on sale of old and new housing
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation proposed to provide ceiling prices on the sale of old and new housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such authority is presented as essential to avert further skyrocketing of home prices; pending bills' price‑control features are described as workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint a housing expediter to coordinate and expedite housing production
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a housing expediter in the Office of War Mobilization and Reconversion to assume responsibility for coordinating and expediting housing production and recommending new steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasked to search out bottlenecks at all levels (industry, local, state, national) and recommend actions as conditions change; formal appointment (Wilson Wyatt) is announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communities establish emergency housing committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Mayors of communities with severe problems are requested to set up emergency housing committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local committees to help returning veterans find homes or, if necessary, emergency shelter; part of decentralized response alongside federal measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend obsolete building codes to permit reasonable use of substitute materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Communities can amend obsolete building codes to permit reasonable use of substitute materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended because some materials will remain scarce for months; intended to allow continued construction using acceptable substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspend nonessential construction to free supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspend all construction that is not immediately necessary to eliminate drain on supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War and Navy Departments were requested to suspend nonessential construction so materials can be diverted to urgent housing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch inventories closely to prevent hoarding and ensure prompt distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventories are to be watched closely to prevent hoarding and thus assure prompt distribution of scarce materials and supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring and possible widening of controls to avoid stockpiling by intermediaries or producers; part of anti‑inflation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain several years of peak housing production
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing less than several years of peak production will really solve the housing problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes need for time to get construction industry into full operation; implies long‑term production targets and workforce scaling (e.g., on‑site workers rising toward levels needed to reach housing unit goals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divert materials from less urgent construction via priority system
rubrics_metrics.description: Divert materials from less urgent commercial and industrial construction and from high‑cost housing through a priority system to increase supply for home‑building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority allocation of scarce materials is presented as one of the few immediate remedies to boost home construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure high proportion of released surplus materials goes to housing (target ≥70%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangements to see that at least 70 per cent of released surplus materials goes into housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special teams to locate and sell surpluses on the spot with distribution rules favoring housing use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure national security plans against WWII lessons and future dangers
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate any plan for future national security by asking (a) What weaknesses revealed by World War II should be corrected? and (b) What new dangers must we anticipate and guard against?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should both correct past defects and meet new technical and strategic dangers (e.g., atomic weapons, rockets) — this is the stated two‑standard test for acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organized integration of foreign and military policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To be acceptable, a plan must establish organized means for the integration of foreign and military policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration is listed as the first of eight explicit requirements for a national security plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizations in being for directing industrial mobilization and reconciling mobilization with national resources
rubrics_metrics.description: To be acceptable, a plan must have organizations in being for directing industrial mobilization and for reconciling industrial mobilization with national resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent organizational means (not ad hoc wartime agencies) are required to prevent waste and disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient organization to translate strategic requirements into matériel and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: A more efficient organization for the translation of strategic requirements into matériel and personnel is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must ensure that strategic needs are converted into concrete procurement and personnel plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate military and other war budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for the coordination of military and other war budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary coordination is necessary to avoid conflicting demands on national resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate waste and duplication between military departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate means for the elimination of waste and duplication in and between the military departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should create mechanisms (e.g., Military Munitions Board) to reduce overlap while recognizing that unification alone does not guarantee elimination of waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an efficient coordinated intelligence organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An efficient coordinated intelligence organization serving government departments and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous and coordinated collection and interpretation of intelligence is listed as a national security requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide organizational means to foster scientific research and development
rubrics_metrics.description: An organizational means for fostering scientific research and development within the military departments and among civilian organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes rapid development and military application of scientific knowledge (e.g., radar, proximity fuses, atomic discoveries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow full opportunity for each military branch to develop specialized capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Full opportunity for each branch of the military services to develop for its specialized task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for separate departments and autonomy (e.g., strategic air force) so each service can be energized and imaginative in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain civilian control of the military through separate departments and civilian heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Civilian authority shall control military authority; continuation of separate departments maintains civilian control by providing each service with a civilian head of Cabinet rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a democratic principle and a check‑and‑balance requirement in the choice of organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralize procurement rather than create single centralized command
rubrics_metrics.description: Decentralize procurement—'not conglomerating'—because wartime experience showed duplication even within 'single command' structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Navy Plan proposes a Military Munitions Board under a civilian chairman to unify procurement where advisable, rather than a single gigantic purchasing organization; warns that merger alone won't eliminate waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a National Security Resources Board to coordinate military, civilian and material needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a National Security Resources Board to correlate military requirements, civilian needs and material resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as the Navy Plan's mechanism to provide three‑way coordination (strategic policy, civilian needs, material resources) and to prevent disruptions to the national economy.
